title: Coding agents badly misjudge task duration and their own results
friendlyTitle: AI coding agents are poor at knowing how long work takes
summary: A MATS research project tested Claude Code and Codex on predicting and retrospectively estimating wall-clock runtime. The agents consistently overestimated duration—especially for short tasks—and older tested models overrated their own work; explicit access to elapsed-time information greatly improved retrospective estimates.
friendlySummary: In these tests, Claude Code and Codex usually predicted much more time than tasks really needed and were too positive about their own results. Giving them a clock helped with time estimates.
whyItMatters: Do not use an agent’s prose estimate as a scheduler or completion signal for long-running automation. Workflows should supply clocks, enforce external time and cost budgets, and decide success from tests or observable outcomes rather than the agent’s self-rating.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use real timers, budgets and tests instead of trusting an agent to say how long it worked or whether it succeeded.
